Initially I thought this was a notification for my agent tasks when they complete but later it turned out to speed up my agents since they simply ping me on my lock screen and I tap to give them the right decision, it's simple and super convenient. #### What needs improvement. Title: Pushary : Pushary Forums | Product Hunt
Control panel for AI agents on your lock screen. # Pushary - Control panel for AI agents. You start a Cursor task, check Twitter, come back 40 minutes later. Your agent finished 35 minutes ago. Pushary sends push notifications to your phone when any AI agent completes, fails, or needs approval. Approve commands from your lock screen. One npx command to set up. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Hermes, Lovable, and any MCP agent. ### Replies. Aadil here, solo founder building Pushary. Here's the thing that bugs me: I run Claude Code on a big refactor, go make coffee, come back 40 minutes later — and the agent finished 35 minutes ago. Or worse, it's been waiting for my permission to run a command the entire time. So I built Pushary, push notifications for AI coding agents. Run `npx @pushary/agent-hooks setup` 2. Pick your agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Hermes, Lovable) 3. Your phone now buzzes when your agent finishes, fails, or needs approval. The permission hooks are the killer feature. Your agent wants to run `rm -rf ./src`? You get a push notification with Allow/Deny buttons. Tap from your lock screen. You never leave the couch. What's different from launch #2: - Permission hooks (approve/deny from your phone) - 3 question types (yes/no, multiple choice, free text) - Works with 6+ agents now (was just Cursor + Claude) - One unified CLI setup (was manual JSON config) Free to start. Would love your feedback, especially if you're running multiple agents and losing time to tab-checking. Turns out the biggest bottleneck in my AI workflow was... me forgetting I had an AI workflow running 😅. Getting notified when Claude finishes or needs approval just feels weirdly natural. Been loving this so far. Simple idea, executed really well 🚀. don't forget to use the code for a month off :).

Title: Pushary : Pushary Forums | Product Hunt
Control panel for AI agents on your lock screen. # Pushary - Get push notifications when your AI agent finishes. Connect Pushary to Cursor, Claude, or Lovable via MCP. Get a push notification the moment your AI task completes. I was spending 10+ hours a day in Cursor. I'd kick off a long agent task, check Twitter for 'one minute,' and come back 40 minutes later. I built Pushary for push notifications (it's a full platform for SaaS/e-commerce). I wired up an MCP server, and now my phone buzzes the second any AI agent completes. 4 lines of JSON in your MCP config. Works with Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, Lovable and anything that speaks MCP. Your phone buzzes when the task is done. Pushary is actually a full push notification platform (80% open rates, HubSpot sync, Shopify recovery, the works). What other AI workflows would you want notifications for? Happy to hear thoughts and comments from you guys how you're getting notified with pushary :). Beyond “task finished,” which agent states ended up being the real time-sinks (e.g., waiting for input/approval, errors, tool timeouts), and how are you detecting those states reliably across different MCP clients? This is exactly the rabbit hole I went down after the initial "task done" notification. 1. **Waiting for human input.** The agent needs a yes/no decision and just sits there. The agent hits a wall and you only find out 20 minutes later. The agent calls this when it finishes a task or hits an error. * **ask\_user\_yes\_no** sends a push notification with a question. You tap yes or no on your phone. Up to 55 seconds, retryable, your answer sticks around for 10 minutes. The MCP tools give the AI a way to reach you. This works across Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, Lovable, and anything that speaks MCP because MCP is the common protocol. "Task done" notifications save you 5-10 minutes per task. @mcarmonas Of course, you just have to add this in a skill/rule file and it asks you a yes/no question like a G. Hey Aadil, tried it and this is exactly what I was looking for.
